### **Job Description and Duties**


Under the direction of the Nutria Eradication Operations Supervisor, the incumbent will support the Department's Nutria Eradication Program. Nutria are highly invasive and extremely detrimental to the environment, but primarily nocturnal and relatively elusive in low densities. This position is physically demanding, but highly rewarding given the ultimate accomplishment of protecting California's wetlands, waterways, infrastructure, and agriculture. As part of a team, the incumbent will contribute to surveys to detect, locate, and trap nutria, with the ultimate goal of eradicating nutria from the state. Duties include: Under the supervision of the Nutria Eradication Operations Supervisor, the incumbent will serve as one of the lead field scientists for the Nutria Eradication Program. Nutria are highly invasive and extremely detrimental to the environment, but primarily nocturnal and relatively elusive in low densities. This position will play a critical role in the coordination of field crews conducting nutria surveys and trapping across the northern portion of the nutria infestation. The incumbent will assist the Operations Supervisor with training, leading, and evaluating field crew technicians and scientific aides to survey for, detect, and remove nutria, with the ultimate goal of eradicating nutria from the State of California. The incumbent will lead the team by example in conducting habitat suitability assessments, visual observation and camera surveys, trapping, and electronic data collection (i.e., ESRI Collector smartphone application), as well as effective use of baits and lures and obtaining entry permits from local landowners. The incumbent is responsible for conducting morning briefings of the assigned crew, tracking daily spatial assignments, and ensuring field staff understand understand project protocols. The incumbent will work with the Operations Supervisors, other field crew leads, and Planning Specialist to evaluate and help refine detection and trapping methods and tools for the most effective and efficient detection and removal of nutria. The incumbent will also closely coordinate with other regions and Department functions, as well as other affected and involved local, State, and Federal agencies. Work includes preparing draft reports and correspondence and answering routine questions from the public relative to Departmental nutria efforts. The primary geographical focus of this position will be in San Joaquin, Sacramento, Contra Costa, Solano, Alameda, and Calaveras counties, but work may be assigned in any part of the area of nutria infestation. This position is physically demanding, but highly rewarding given the ultimate accomplishment of protecting California's wetlands, waterways, infrastructure, and agriculture from the devastation nutria have caused in other regions of North America. Incumbent must be willing and able to competently use firearms as per the Department’s Policy for Non\-Enforcement Personnel.  

  

  



**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4\.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:

Link to Environmental Scientist Exam: CalCareers

### **Working Conditions**


Be willing to work atypical hours and on weekends. Some overnight travel (\<5%) may be required. Able to swim, walk through deep mud and thick vegetation, work on steep or uneven terrain, in extreme weather and under physically challenging conditions. Be willing and able to competently use pellet pistols or firearms as per the Department’s Policy for Non\-Enforcement Personnel. Willing to handle live animals and carcasses, dispatch animals, and conduct simple tissue sampling and necropsies. Possess valid Driver's License and be able to safely and effectively operate watercraft and Utility Task Vehicles (UTV)s, as well as tow trailers. This job requires daily operation of State vehicles to reach field sites, regular use of kayaks, and occasional operation of UTVs and motorized watercraft. Must wear Department uniform.  

  

Be willing and able to obtain a California Boater Card and other motorboat operator certifications as determined necessary.  

  

The primary geographical focus of this position will be in San Joaquin, Sacramento, Contra Costa, Solano, Alameda, and Calaveras counties, but work may be assigned in any part of the area of nutria infestation.

We are an award\-winning California\-based environmental consulting firm with 550\+ professionals and more than 30 years of diverse experience serving clients in transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, private development, and government sectors. Rincon Consultants, Inc. is seeking a **Principal or Director, Stormwater \& Watershed Sciences** to lead and grow our construction and industrial stormwater quality services throughout California.


This senior leadership role will focus on developing client programs related to California’s Construction and Industrial General Permits compliance, stormwater monitoring, SWPPP development and BMP implementation, regulatory strategy, and program management. ### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you looking to make a difference and join a highly motivated team working on issues critical to ensuring the safety and sustainability of California? The Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety’s Environmental Science Division is seeking an Environmental Scientist to analyze performance with vegetation management commitments in electrical utility Wildfire Mitigation Plans (WMP).
  

The Environmental Science Division is responsible for evaluating the vegetation management aspects of utility WMPs, assessing performance in meeting vegetation management\-related commitments described in the WMPs, and ensuring that each utility is reducing its risk of igniting a catastrophic wildfire. To this end, Division scientists review regulatory filings and utility procedures, analyze reported data, perform audits, conduct field inspections, publish findings, and engage with the utilities and interested parties. Division scientists serve as subject\-matter experts in utility vegetation management and environmental policy related to wildfire risk reduction. Our team of scientists is highly collaborative and works closely with the Performance Assessment, Electric Safety Policy, and Data Analytics Divisions.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM
has a unique opportunity for a Project Manager to build upon their technical and management skills within our Environmental business line to be based in one of our AECOM offices in Northern California. Project Managers are responsible for overseeing the performance of a group of projects/portfolios to assure the achievement of internal and client facing KPIs and project goals .
The position requires an especially accomplished individual to interface with clients, lead and support business development opportunities, and lead/influence solutions and strategies for a portfolio of remediation sites. Applicants with verifiable experience in technical roles performing and managing investigation/cleanup of contaminants of concern are highly preferred.

The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:

Project Delivery
:
Manages projects, directs data analysis and reporting for specific environmental project tasks and guide site remediation strategies bringing sites to closure
Collaborates and participate in technical discussions with project team members
Adheres to AECOM’s Quality Management System (QMS) in execution of projects and portfolios
Interacts with various state agencies to develop favorable risk-based remediation goals
Develops and maintains communication channels with clients, stake holders, and internal project teams
Develops and formulate solutions to client problems/issues
Participates in project reviews of major program/project dashboards/deep dives to identify issues and improve performance
Embraces workflow optimization and adoption of digital tools
Actively integrates global resources into project delivery and manages the change associated with this transition
Organically grow current portfolios through exceptional project delivery and client relationships

Operations:

Drive business performance and the attainment and exceedance of internal KPIs
Assist Program Manager to maintain departmental compliance with Business Line Pricing guidance and DOA approval framework
Assist Program Manager to ensure the accuracy of the department’s sales pipeline data
Participate in proposal development to support business growth
Acts as a point of escalation for project issues and makes recommendations to improve performance. This may include addressing project resourcing gaps, supporting technical issues, resolving invoicing and cash collection challenges, addressing subconsultant and vendor concerns, etc.

People:

Builds, maintains, and facilitates trusting relationships with key contacts across the depth and breadth of client organizations
Directs and coordinates work assignments and review performance to ensure the efficient, cost-effective utilization of staff
Promotes health and safety stewardship, including performing local field visit

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

BA/BS within any Engineering, Business, Environmental Science Fields of study, and (4) four years of relevant work experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
Ability to travel for on-site meetings and to develop client relationships
Valid Driver's License, subject to a pre-employment Motor Vehicle Record Screening as well as background check.
US citizenship or permanent residency is required. Sponsorship at this time or in the future will not be available for this role.

Preferred Qualifications

10+ years overall professional experience
PG or PE preferred
Verifiable experience in prominent roles performing and managing investigation/remediation of chemical / industrial / refining sites
Previous leadership and/or management experience
Ability to influence others and move toward a common vision or goal
Master's Degree a plus in Geology, Engineering, Science or related field
Excellent client management skills
Detail oriented with strong organizational and communication skills (both verbal and written)
Superior communication skills (writing, editing, and reporting) for a wide variety of audiences.
Experience in team management and scheduling of staff and resources to ensure on time and on budget project delivery
Experience preparing proposals, cost estimates, schedules, and change orders
Strong project management skills and a strategic perspective
Excellent business analytics and organizational skills preferable
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities
Strong understanding and has led professional teams in executing Site Investigations, Remedial Investigations, Feasibility Studies, Risk Assessment, and Treatability Studies

Additional Information

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $110000 to $130000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

The Regulatory Development Section (RDS) within the Monitoring and Laboratory Division (MLD) is seeking a highly skilled Staff Air Pollution Specialist to help implement a multi\-agency pilot program involving the repurposing of crude oil and natural gas wells and production infrastructure for energy storage and generation.  

Senate Bill (SB) 567, authored by Senator Monique Limón and signed into law in October of 2025, establishes the Gravity Based Energy Storage Well Pilot Program, which will sunset on January 1, 2035\. It authorizes the conversion of 250 idle crude oil and natural gas wells to gravity\-based energy storage systems. Under SB 567, CARB will collaborate with the Department of Conservation, California Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) and the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) to establish criteria for mechanical integrity testing, continuous leak monitoring of air pollutants, and reporting protocols. CARB will also serve as a key technical and policy advisor alongside CalGEM, SWRCB, and interested parties to evaluate the pilot’s progress and to include recommendations whether to continue the Gravity\-Based Energy Storage Well Program.  

Duties include: 1\) providing leadership and direction in the review and evaluation of monitoring technologies which could be applied to the continuous monitoring of toxic air pollutants from leaks; 2\) leading a multi disciplinary team of engineers and specialists within CARB to develop guidelines for the pilot program, which will include elements such as continuous leak detection performance standards, data reporting and assisting CalGEM in reviewing and determining if plans submitted by the operators comply with the guidelines; 3\) facilitating stakeholder engagement activities, explaining complex technical requirements in plain english, leading meetings with interested stakeholders such as community groups, oil and gas operators, and the public; 4\) working with CalGEM and SWRCB to evaluate the results of the pilot program and recommending if a Gravity\-Based Energy Storage Well Program along with conditions should be made permanent.

### **Job Description and Duties**


This position is a special and unique opportunity to work in some of the most beautiful watersheds in the state of California, studying and enhancing salmon and steelhead populations primarily in the Eel River and watersheds of the Mendocino Coast. Work is related to state and federal Endangered Species Act listed stocks and management of valued fisheries for the state and tribes on the North Coast. Promoting collaboration with partners in order to leverage collective resources is encouraged. This position stands to make a positive and real difference for trust resources and those that value them. Under the general guidance of the Coastal Fisheries Environmental Program Manager, the incumbent supervises the Coastal Watershed Planning and Assessment Program. The Program includes a broad suite of monitoring, assessment, restoration, and regulatory activities in Humboldt and Mendocino Counties. These activities include monitoring and assessment of fish life history, fish distribution, recovery, permitting, ecosystem assessment, restoration planning, and annual sportfish regulations. This position will oversee or support various aquatic resource plans, restoration and monitoring plans, and several monitoring and assessment activities related specifically to the Eel River and potential dam removal. The incumbent manages a complex budget, helps develop and manage large scale ecosystem assessments, and develops and manages complex contracts or grants with ecological scope. As such the position entails significant grant/contract writing and management responsibilities. This includes planning, directing, and coordinating all aspects of development and implementation of detailed and watershed\-specific monitoring and research programs for salmon, steelhead, and other trout populations. Responsibilities are varied and include analyzing complex environmental issues, requiring a high level of personal initiative in the application of sound scientific methods and ecological principles to natural resource assessment, management, planning and habitat restoration activities. Incumbent will represent the Department in dealings with local, State and federal governmental agencies, Tribal partners, conservation groups and private landowners. Area of geographic responsibility includes all nine Northern California counties that make up the Northern Region, however duties will be largely focused in Humboldt and Mendocino Counties. Performance of specified duties requires a comprehensive knowledge of administrative procedures, Department policies, applicable environmental law, and complex ecological principals. Contacts made in the course of this work are highly sensitive and involve a wide degree of interests. The level of consequence of error in applying the best available scientific knowledge, technical information, and policy may have highly significant and adverse consequences. Description

Environmental Chemist

Put your analytical skills toward making a positive impact on the planet and your career! Join ICF in support of the US Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) contract at the new Region 9 Laboratory in Corvallis, Oregon.

ICF is looking for an Environmental Laboratory Chemist in support of the USEPA Region 9 Environmental Services Assistance Team (ESAT) contract. ESAT provides analytical, quality assurance (QA), and technical support to USEPA programs such as Superfund and other programs requiring the identification, assessment, remediation, and regulation of environmental hazards. The team performs analysis on soil, water, air, waste, and tissue samples for chemical contaminants using USEPA-approved methods supporting EPA’s mission to protect human health and the environment through programs such as the Drinking Water programs, Clean Water Act (CWA), Clean Air Act (CAA), Superfund (CERCLA).

The Environmental Chemist
will apply their knowledge and work experience to primarily support the preparation and analysis of organic chemistry methods with possible cross-training on various inorganic analyses. All team activities must comply with EPA methods for various media (air, water, soil, biota) and environmental programs as well as the NELAC standard (2016). Job duties include sample preparation in support of and operation of GC-ECD, GC-FID, and GCMS to determine volatile and semivolatile organic compounds, pesticides, Aroclors, and fuel hydrocarbon as well as new and emerging contaminants. The successful candidate must be able to work both independently and as member of a team.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, environmental science, environmental engineering, or related.
4+ years of laboratory experience using EPA-approved methodologies and instrumentation, preferably GC-FID, GC-ECD and GC/MS.
Excellent verbal, interpersonal and written communication skills, and the ability to think critically.
U.S. citizenship required per federal contract.
MUST BE ABLE TO PASS an EPA background check to obtain access to US federal property.

Preferred Qualifications

Solvent extraction experience using EPA methodologies and CLLE, SPE, ASE and other techniques.
2-5 years of progressive experience in laboratories accredited for environmental analyses (e.g., TNI or NELAC, state programs).
Experience working at Federal facilities.
Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) experience, knowledge of Promium Element LIMS is a plus.

Job Overview:

At the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, we deliver reliable water to a region with 19 million people—and to accomplish this, we rely on a team of talented employees: innovators, problem\-solvers, and collaborators who make it all possible.  

This recruitment may result in an **Eligibility List\***.  

The Environmental Specialist serves as an advanced, journey\-level technical expert responsible for planning, conducting, coordinating, and monitoring complex environmental studies and projects for the Metropolitan Water District.  

At this recognized specialist level, you will be responsible for ensuring compliance with source and treated water regulations with a strong focus on invasive mussel control and emerging regulations. You will spearhead the agency's strategic response to invasive mussels in source waters and ensure compliance with relevant environmental and water quality regulations, California Department of Fish and Wildlife mandates, and invasive species frameworks.  

You will also be responsible for tracking and ensuring compliance with environmental permitting and pesticide regulations, considerations for raw water releases, contributing to agency responses to federal and state regulatory developments, hazardous waste management, various aspects of source water protection, and preparing reports, response plans, and research proposals.  

Daily duties include monitoring pertinent environmental laws, codes, regulations, and pending litigation that impact operations, as well as drafting actionable, high\-level strategies and responses to address operational requirements and regulatory developments.  

Candidates must possess a bachelor's degree in environmental science, biology, chemistry, or a related field, supplemented by six years of progressive, professional environmental compliance experience that demonstrates mastery over multi\-agency coordination and permitting and complex project management. **What You’ll Do:*** Lead agency response to invasive mussels in source water infrastructure.
* Develop control strategies to prevent and mitigate infrastructure and biological impacts.
* Coordinate monitoring programs for invasive species.
* Ensure compliance with state and federal water quality, environmental, and invasive species regulations.

**The Opportunity:**


Tetra Tech, Inc is currently seeking a motivated, detail\-oriented Entry\-Level Environmental Specialist to support environmental consulting projects across a range of sectors, including regulatory compliance, field investigations, environmental permitting, and reporting. This position is ideal for a recent graduate or early\-career professional who is eager to build a career in environmental consulting and contribute to meaningful projects that support responsible development and environmental stewardship.

**Why Tetra Tech:**


At Tetra Tech, we are *Leading with Science* to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry\-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting\-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

**Your Impact:**


Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting\-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world\-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

**Essential Job Functions:**


The Environmental Specialist will work under the guidance of experienced staff and project managers to assist with field work, data collection, technical documentation, and client deliverables. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong communication skills, a willingness to learn, and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team.

* Support preparation of technical reports, permit applications, compliance documents, and environmental deliverables.
* Collect, organize, and analyze environmental data in support of project requirements.
* Conduct literature and regulatory research related to environmental permitting and compliance.
* Maintain accurate field notes, logs, and project documentation.
* Follow health, safety, and quality assurance protocols during field and office work.
* Support senior staff with project coordination, scheduling, and client communication as needed.
* Travel to project sites as required for field assignments.
* Perform other duties as assigned.


**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Biology, Geology, Natural Resources, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
* 0–2 years of relevant experience, including internships, co\-ops, or field research.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, especially Word, Excel, and Outlook.
* Ability to organize information, manage multiple tasks, and meet deadlines.
* Willingness to work outdoors in varying weather and field conditions.
* Ability to communicate effectively in person, by phone, and by email in field and office settings.
* A Pre\-employment drug screening in compliance with state regulations is required.
* Must possess a valid driver's license with a clean driving record without restrictions.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Interest in NEPA, CEQA, ESA, CWA.

**Physical Requirements:**

* Occasional travel, including day travel and overnight stays (approx. 25\-50% of travel required).
* Ability to lift, carry, and transport field equipment and supplies, typically up to 25–50 pounds.
* Exposure to uneven terrain, mud, rocks, standing water, vegetation, and other natural site hazards may occur. Noise, vibration, odors, and airborne dust may be present at some project sites.
* Personal protective equipment may be required depending on site conditions and project scope. Ability to wear required personal protective equipment, including hard hats, safety glasses, gloves, high\-visibility vests, steel\-toe boots, and respiratory protection if needed.
* Ability to walk, stand, and/or hike for extended periods, often on uneven or rough terrain. Ability to bend, kneel, crouch, climb, and reach as needed during field activities.
* Ability to sit for extended periods when performing office\-based tasks such as report writing, data entry, and analysis.

**Work Environment / Environmental Factors:**

* Fieldwork may occur outdoors in a variety of weather conditions, including heat, cold, wind, rain, snow, and dust. Field locations may include construction sites, industrial facilities, undeveloped land, wetlands, streams, roadways, or remote project areas.
* Work may involve exposure to traffic, heavy equipment, moving machinery, or active construction operations.
* Position is based out of the Ranco Cordova, CA or Phoenix, AZ office location. Potential of a hybrid work arrangement but the candidate must reside within 20 miles of the local office. This arrangement is subject to review and may change at the company’s discretion.

**Additional Information:**

* Full\-time, Monday through Friday work schedule (40 hours). Hours may vary based on project demands, weather conditions, or client schedules. Some work may require early mornings, evenings, or weekend assignments.
* Work is performed in both office and field settings.

**Target salary range: $24\.00 / hour to $25\.00 / hour.** Please note that Tetra Tech considers various factors in determining pay, including but not limited to: education, relevant and demonstrated work experience in the role, skills, geographic location, qualifications, certifications, and other competencies relevant to the needs of the business.

* Comprehensive and market\-competitive benefits.

### **Job Description and Duties**


The California Coastal Commission is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist or Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to join its Ecology Team (Technical Services Unit) at its Headquarters Office in downtown San Francisco. This position will primarily focus on the relationship between wildfire and coastal ecology as relates to vegetation management for fuel reduction, ecological restoration, and resilience work across a range of ecosystems, including forests, shrublands, grasslands and wetlands throughout the coastal zone, which extends inland from the shoreline at variable distances up to more than five miles in some areas.


The Commission is a small State agency that is charged with protecting coastal resources and managing coastal development in California. The Commission’s mission is to implement the Coastal Act and to protect, restore, and enhance coastal and marine resources for the continuing benefit of current and future generations. It carries out this mandate through regulatory and planning actions related to development within offshore waters and on land along the California coast. The Commission also has authority under the federal Coastal Zone Management Act to review federal and federally\-permitted activities such as dredging, military training exercises, wildland management, and highway projects that affect resources of the coastal zone.


The Ecology Team generally supports the Commission and its staff with technical review and analysis of potential effects on the coast’s sensitive natural resources associated with proposed development projects. Under the direction of the Ecology Team Manager, the successful incumbent will be integrated into the existing team of five ecologists and work with Commission staff to address ecological issues raised in the Commission’s policy, planning, and regulatory work as relates to wildfire resilience and risk reduction efforts. This work will focus on understanding and addressing the ecological effects of vegetation management for fuel reduction and wildfire resilience, including through ecological restoration, throughout the coastal zone. It will necessitate cooperation with other scientific and technical teams such as Mapping and Water Quality, coordination with the Commission’s Statewide Planning Unit, and provision of scientific support to staff and the Commission. Duties will be adjusted commensurately to the level at which the position is filled. Generally, the incumbent will be expected to: review and analyze a variety of technical reports including CEQA/NEPA documents, technical surveys and memoranda, restoration and mitigation plans, and scientific literature; conduct research and investigations often involving complex environmental conditions and circumstances; identify problems including potential adverse impacts to coastal resources and means to avoid and minimize these; factor in climate change dynamics relative to environmental considerations; coordinate with other federal, state, and local agencies; and, make recommendations for conformance with the natural resource policies of the Coastal Act and relevant certified plans.


Key functions of the job include: analyzing proposed fire resilience and risk reduction work for consistency with applicable Coastal Act policies; tracking topical scientific literature including white papers and peer\-reviewed publications; guiding related policy based on scientific understanding of the issues and existing frameworks; developing recommendations on how to avoid and minimize adverse impacts to native habitat (including for communities and species) associated with fuel reduction and vegetation management efforts across the landscape while advancing ecological resilience; contributing to the development of recommendations for Commission regulatory action, including staff reports, permit conditions, and planning documents; communicating with project proponents; updating and maintaining a spatial database of authorized fire resilience and risk reduction work and conducting geospatial analyses; reviewing monitoring and mitigation plans and reports; participating in site visits and inspections to evaluate on\-the\-ground ecological conditions; writing technical memoranda to support and accompany staff reports and recommendations; and providing technical presentations at public meetings. The incumbent may also represent the Commission staff on multi\-agency work groups, task forces, and similar entities; and coordinate with staff of local, state, and federal agencies; the legislature; stakeholder groups; and the broader public.


The position offers considerable opportunity for developing and contributing expertise on a range of ecosystems as well as relevant and emerging issues related to coastal ecology and wildfire resilience in California’s coastal landscape.

At the Oregon Health Authority (OHA), we value diversity and encourage applicants from all backgrounds and experiences to help us build a stronger, more equitable future for all.

Opportunity Awaits, Apply Today!
– Health Physicist- Licensing (Environmental Health Specialist 3)

The Oregon Health Authority (OHA), Public Health Division (PHD), Radiation Protection Services section is seeking a Health Physicist – Licensing (Environmental Health Specialist 3) to join its team.

In this role, the Health Physicist will provide guidance to public and private sector officials on radiation health and safety issues, drawing on environmental testing data and scientific research. This individual will interpret and explain applicable statutes, rules, policies, and procedures to licensees and applicants. They will also review radiation safety program requirements, identify areas within license applications that may require clarification or improvement, and offer appropriate recommendations. In addition, the position provides instruction to individuals or groups of licensees on the methods and procedures necessary to comply with regulatory standards.

For a full review of the position description, please
click here
.

What We Are Looking For

Minimum Qualifications:
These qualifications must be reflected in your application for consideration.

Two years of experience equivalent to an Environmental Health Specialist 2 working under general supervision of an environmental health specialist, conducting environmental health or hazardous materials investigations, inspecting facilities and equipment for environmental health regulation compliance, investigating and assessing the impact of adverse environmental conditions on the public health, preparing health permits, conducting studies and surveys, and developing solutions to environmental problems AND

A bachelor's degree with 45 quarter (30 semester) hours in a field of science.

Desired Attributes:
The following are desired attributes that we have identified as key to success for this role at OHA. These are the attributes we are looking for in our top candidate. If you possess any of these attributes, please highlight them in your application, resume, and address specifically in your cover letter.

Experience in advising public and private officials on radiation health and safety issues.
Experience in interpreting rules, policies, and procedures to radioactive material licensees.
Experience in reviewing the licensee’s radiation safety program and assessing needs for improvement.
Experience in providing methods and procedures for compliance with regulatory requirements.
Experience working with external partners, licensees and other local, state and federal agencies.
Ability to evaluate license applications and communicate with prospective licensees regarding missing information or clarification of supplied information.
Experience working with software such as Microsoft Office Suite, Word, Excel, Access and PowerPoint.

Preference Statement:
Preference will be given to candidates possessing more years of experience and meeting more of the desired attributes.

About Us

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real-world impact.

“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.

When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.

Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.

A Day in the Life

Formerly known as Epic Environmental, the Australian arm of Onterris has kept the strong culture we are well known for. The team continues to work closely with clients, building trusted relationships and delivering high-quality outcomes without an overemphasis on KPIs.

Our teams have the opportunity to work alongside industry leaders, auditors, and professionals with vast experience within our industry, while enjoying regular social events and collaborative work that bring the team together. Onterris also supports career development through relevant internal opportunities and individual one-on-one career conversations focused on growth and progression.

Responsibilities

We are seeking a Principal Environmental Scientist to join our Assessment and Approvals team, working our in thriving Brisbane office where you will be responsible for a full range of activities including:

Performing business development by bringing in new clients to the business
Presenting and leading external meetings with clients
Successfully managing multiple projects at any one time
Developing and reviewing quality management systems
Mentoring and training junior staff

Your Expertise And Skills

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.

15+ years of experience within environmental consulting
Tertiary qualifications from a recognised institute in Environmental Science or related field
In-depth knowledge of environmental approvals and impact assessments for the Queensland resources sector
Proven experience with EIS, PRCP and EA approvals

Onterris is a leading global environmental solutions company partnering with organizations to solve complex challenges where environmental pressures, regulatory expectations and operational risks intersect. Guided by our mission to advance the way of life without compromising the integrity of our environment, we believe environmental responsibility and human progress are fundamentally connected. \-

This position will focus on recycling compliance programs relating to non\-hazardous materials and will spend a majority of time providing technical assistance, inspections, and enforcement within the community, including program development and record keeping. The ideal candidate enjoys a variety of work environments and tasks, including physical outdoor labor, an office environment, and regular interaction with the public.  

*This is a Monday \- Friday in\-office position, and occasional weekend and after hours work.* *This position is non\-exempt and represented by the Local 39 IUOE union.*

**Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water****Reference number**
552626**Occupation**

From AUD $110,000\.00 to $119,999\.00 per year**Closing date**

***Do you want your work to make a difference for NSW?***  

*Working to protect the state’s environment and heritage.*  

* **Protect NSW's environment through science**
* **Permanent full\-time opportunity, 35 hours per week**
* **Lidcombe office, hybrid working supported**
* **Salary relative to experience, and ranges from $112,375 to $124,158 pa \+ super**

  


Join a passionate team of scientists making a significant impact on environmental protection! Our Science and Insights team is seeking to appoint a Scientist (Ecotoxicology). This is your chance to apply your expertise to important scientific programs and projects and engage in meaningful work that addresses pressing ecotoxicological issues.  

  

**About the role**  

As a Scientist (Ecotoxicology), you will contribute to the design, delivery and analysis of ecotoxicology projects that inform environmental decision\-making and regulation. Working alongside experienced scientists and technical experts, you will support investigations into environmental incidents and research programs, perform ecotoxicity testing, analyse and interpret ecotoxicological data, prepare scientific reports and presentations and collaborate with government agencies, research institutions and other stakeholders to deliver high\-quality environmental outcomes.  

  

The Ecotoxicology team collaborates closely with the Chemical Forensics team, together forming the Environmental Forensics Unit. The role of the Environmental Forensics Unit is to investigate pollution incidents, provide expert advice, and conduct research to protect the New South Wales community, economy and environment from the risk posed by current and legacy environmental contaminants.  

  

This is an exciting opportunity to apply your scientific expertise to real\-world environmental challenges within a collaborative, supportive and knowledge\-driven team. To further strengthen our programs and projects, we provide professional development opportunities and support special interest projects that can enhance the capability and services the Ecotoxicology team provides.  

  

**About You**  

You are a curious and motivated scientist with qualifications and experience in ecotoxicology, including ecotoxicity testing, data analysis and interpretation. You enjoy solving complex environmental problems with scientific rigour and are comfortable working independently or as part of a team. Strong analytical thinking, attention to detail, and effective communication skills will enable you to thrive in this role and contribute to protecting the environment for future generations.  

  

**Essential Requirements**
* Scientific qualifications, knowledge and demonstrated experience in ecotoxicology science including ecotoxicity methods, analysis and interpretation.

  


For more information read the full Role Description: **Scientist (Ecotoxicology)**  

  

**About the Team – Science \& Insights**  

Science \& Insights sits within the **NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW),** which works to protect the state’s environment and heritage while driving a sustainable future for NSW.  

  

Working at the intersection of science, policy and delivery, Science \& Insights collaborates across government, academia, industry and communities to identify priority issues and deliver practical, high\-impact solutions.  

  

The division brings together six specialist branches spanning conservation and restoration, climate and atmospheric science, environmental protection, remote sensing and landscape science, science impact and assessment, and water, wetlands and coastal science.  

  

Together, these teams provide the evidence, expertise and insights needed to understand NSW’s environment, manage risks and drive sustainable outcomes.  

  

The division’s work is focused on building a strong evidence base, advancing innovation in how data is gathered and used, and translating complex scientific information into clear, actionable insights and advice. Through scientific rigour, partnerships and knowledge sharing, Science \& Insights plays a critical role in protecting, restoring and strengthening the resilience of NSW’s environment for future generations.  

  

**Who we are**  

The Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) works to protect the state’s environment and heritage. It leads the way on climate change, driving the sustainable transition to a net zero economy, powered by affordable, reliable, and clean energy.  

  

DCCEEW conserves and protects the state’s natural environment. It manages the NSW national park estate, including its rich and diverse biodiversity and Aboriginal cultural heritage for future generations.  

  

DCCEEW also ensures sustainable management of water resources across the state, to support the environment, communities and industry.  

  

We acknowledge the ongoing custodial responsibilities of the Aboriginal peoples of NSW to care for Country and water and are committed to establishing meaningful partnerships with Aboriginal peoples in the management of the environment.  

  

**To Apply**  

If excited by the information above, we look forward to receiving your application, including a copy of your resume (maximum three pages) and cover letter (maximum two page) expressing your interest and suitability for the role.  

  

Please note to be eligible to apply for this position you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident, or hold a valid Australian working Visa for the duration of the appointment.  

  

**Applications close 13 September 2026 at 11:55PM.**

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. jobs.description:
Company Description

Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

Job Description

We're looking for an Environmental Data Specialist.
You will perform data entry and data management following established business processes to retrieve, verify, and maintain data generated during environmental site characterization, remediation, and monitoring activities. Work with database users, technical field teams, and contract laboratories to receive, assess, and process data; enhance data integrity, accessibility, and usability across one or more functional areas. The position is in the Program Services & Operations Division of the Environmental Restoration Department (ERD).

This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization.

You will

Perform data entry and data management following established business processes to retrieve, verify and maintain data generated during environmental site characterization, remediation, and monitoring activities.
Collaborate with stakeholders to define data requirements, reporting needs, and document them in clear specifications.
Work with technical staff to troubleshoot data issues, coordinate testing, and validate changes or enhancements to data systems and interfaces.
Develop and produce standard, recurring, and ad hoc reports, including data validation and explanation of trends or anomalies.
Assist in designing and implementing improvements to data collection, storage, and retrieval processes, including configuration of data management tools or applications.
Contribute to data-management documentation, including data dictionaries, standard operating procedures, records archives, and data-repositories, and support user training on data-entry standards, reporting tools, and data-management best practices.
Ensure chain-of-custody (COC) forms are complete, accurate, and timely and that the data from the analytical laboratories adhere to the contract.
Monitor data quality metrics and assist in developing controls, checks, and procedures to ensure accuracy, consistency, and completeness of data.
Assist in developing environmental sampling plans and contributing to environmental regulatory reports.
Perform Technical Release Representative (TRR) duties to release work to outside vendors, commit substantial financial resources, and process and pay subcontract analytical laboratory invoices.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship.
Bachelor’s degree in business, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and related experience.
Extensive knowledge of and experience with data management systems related to data entry and verification.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, accuracy, and follow through; experience with techniques for maintaining data integrity, error cause and effect analysis, and error prevention.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with experience to anticipate, identify, and resolve complex problems effectively.
Experience analyzing electronic data deliverables and creating standard and ad hoc reports.
Proven written and verbal communication skills necessary for effective interactions with all levels of personnel internal and external, regulatory agencies, and vendors, and experience working effectively independently and as a member of a team.
Knowledge of and experience using computer programs, system software and computer equipment, such as Microsoft Excel, Oracle based applications, SQL, Apple/Mac, and Linux operating systems.

Qualifications We Desire

Knowledge of LLNL procurement policies and procedures and best business practices.
Experience working with TEIMS, knowledge of SPACT, and ERD’s data repositories (i.e. Data Cave and Data Alley) and LLNL Records Management.
Familiarity with chemistry nomenclature to understand analytical laboratory test results.

Pay Range

$95,820 - $117,312 Annually

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Additional Information

Position Information

This is a Career Indefinite position, open to Lab employees and external candidates.

Why Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory?

Included in 2026 Best Places to Work by Glassdoor!
Flexible Benefits Package
401(k)
Relocation Assistance
Education Reimbursement Program
Flexible schedules (*depending on project needs)
Our values - visit https://www.llnl.gov/inclusion/our-values

Security Clearance

This position requires a Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance. If you are selected, we will initiate a Federal background investigation to determine if you meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information or matter. Also, all L or Q cleared employees are subject to random drug testing. Q-level clearance requires U.S. citizenship.

Pre-Employment Drug Test

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. This includes, but not limited to cell phones, tablets, fitness devices, wireless headphones, and other Bluetooth/wireless enabled devices.

If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.

How To Identify Fake Job Advertisements

Please be aware of recruitment scams where people or entities are misusing the name of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) to post fake job advertisements. LLNL never extends an offer without a personal interview and will never charge a fee for joining our company. All current job openings are displayed on the Career Page under “Find Your Job” of our website. If you have encountered a job posting or have been approached with a job offer that you suspect may be fraudulent, we strongly recommend you do not respond.

To learn more about recruitment scams: https://www.llnl.gov/sites/www/files/2023-05/LLNL-Job-Fraud-Statement-Updated-4.26.23.pdf

Equal Employment Opportunity

We are an equal opportunity employer that is committed to providing all with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, marital status, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, protected veteran status, age, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws.

Reasonable Accommodation

Our goal is to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates applying and interviewing at the Laboratory. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please use our online form to submit a request.

California Privacy Notice

The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) grants privacy rights to all California residents. The law also entitles job applicants, employees, and non-employee workers to be notified of what personal information LLNL collects and for what purpose. The Employee Privacy Notice can be accessed here.

Job Description

Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine is recruiting for a Technical Product Owner – Toxicology Systems
, located in Spring House, PA (US), La Jolla, CA (US) or Beerse, Belgium.

Please note that this role is available across multiple countries and may be posted under different requisition numbers to comply with local requirements. While you are welcome to apply to any or all of the postings, we recommend focusing on the specific country(s) that align with your preferred location(s):

United States (Spring House or La Jolla) - Requisition Number: R-094926
Belgium (Beerse) - Requisition Number: R-096026

The Technology Product Owner for Toxicology will own the technical delivery and support of toxicology products directly supporting toxicology and compound promiscuity science. This business technology role combines deep domain and technical expertise with program-level coordination: you will define technical strategy, own roadmaps and delivery for platforms and models used by toxicology scientists, and act as the primary technical partner and escalation point for scientific stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the technology strategy, roadmap, prioritization, and delivery for digital products supporting toxicology workflows, aligning scientific needs, enterprise technology standards, and available delivery capacity.
Translate scientific needs into technical requirements, success criteria, and measurable deliverables; ensure clear acceptance criteria and productization pathways.
Provide hands-on technical leadership when it adds the most value, including architecture definition, rapid prototyping, design reviews, and evaluation of pipelines and models; coordinate delivery across engineering, data, quality, and scientific partner teams.
Ensure robust data ingestion, normalization, annotation, and QC processes; drive integrations with LIMS, ELN, assay instruments, and third-party data providers.
Define and promote fit-for-purpose practices for data provenance, metadata standards, FAIR principles, and auditability to support scientific reproducibility and applicable compliance requirements.
Act as primary technical liaison for toxicology scientists: capture requirements, demo solutions, gather feedback, and drive adoption.
Lead technical evaluations of vendors and third-party solutions, provide due diligence and risk assessments, and coordinate integrations with procurement, legal, cybersecurity, quality, and engineering partners.
Communicate product status, value, trade-offs, dependencies, and technical risks to leadership and cross-functional stakeholders; facilitate decisions and escalate issues when appropriate.

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Bioinformatics, Computational Chemistry, Toxicology, or related field required; Master’s or PhD preferred.
5+ years of experience supporting scientific research platforms
Demonstrated depth in designing, delivering, and sustaining data platforms, analytics products, or machine learning solutions in life sciences, drug discovery, or another complex scientific environment.
Demonstrated track record of leading technical programs or major projects end-to-end in a complex organization.
Scientific literacy in toxicology and compound promiscuity concepts: assay types, ADME endpoints and off-target profiling.
Maintain sufficient software and data engineering depth to guide solution design, evaluate implementation quality, and contribute directly when needed, including experience with Python or R, SQL, REST APIs, containerization, CI/CD practices, and cloud environments.
Systems and architecture skills: ability to design scalable, maintainable platforms that meet scientists’ needs and regulatory constraints.
Product and delivery leadership: define product outcomes, shape roadmaps, prioritize investments, establish success measures, manage dependencies and risks, and align cross-functional partners around delivery decisions.
Operational leadership: establish support models, service expectations, lifecycle plans, and escalation paths for production solutions; use reliability, adoption, quality, and value measures to guide continuous improvement.
Executive-ready communication and influence: explain technical choices, business value, delivery trade-offs, and risk to scientific, technology, and leadership audiences; build alignment and drive decisions without direct authority.
Strong problem-solving mindset and bias for pragmatic, evidence-driven solutions.

Preferred

Advanced degree (MS/PhD) in toxicology, cheminformatics, computational chemistry, or related discipline.
Hands-on experience with cheminformatics tooling (e.g., RDKit), molecular representations, fingerprints, SMARTS/substructure filtering, and selectivity/promiscuity scoring approaches.
Experience with ML libraries and frameworks (scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch) and MLOps tools (model registries, monitoring).
Prior experience in regulated or GLP-relevant environments, or with quality frameworks that apply to scientific data and software.
Experience performing technical vendor evaluations and managing third-party scientific data/software integrations.

Growth & Diverse Opportunities

AECOM's Water team is delivering some of the most significant water projects across Australia and New Zealand, backed by a record pipeline of work and the strength of our global network. From major flood resilience and water security programs to renewable energy, transport and critical infrastructure projects, our teams are helping shape more sustainable and resilient communities.

As we continue to grow, we're seeking talented Water Resources professionals who want to work on industry-leading projects, collaborate with experts across the globe, and build a rewarding long-term career with AECOM.

With opportunities coming up across Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide, Brisbane, Perth, Newcastle, Gold Coast, Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch
, you can be based from flexible locations Australia and New Zealand offices while contributing to projects of regional, national and international significance.

We welcome interest from professionals across the broader Water Resources sector. Whether your expertise lies in technical delivery, project leadership, modelling, planning or design, we'd love to hear from you.

A market-leading pipeline of Water Resources projects
Opportunities to work across Australia, New Zealand and globally

jobs.title: Alameda Creek Watershed Center Programs and Operations Manager (0922) – Natural Resources and Lands Management Division (Sunol, CA) – SFPUC (167137)
jobs.description:
About

This is a Position-Based Test conducted in accordance with CSC Rule 111A.

Application Opening Date: August 25, 2026
Application Filing Deadline: Application filing will be open at least through September 1, 2026 at 11:59PM (PDT), and will close any time thereafter
Location: 505 Paloma Way, Sunol, CA 94586
Recruitment ID: PBT-0922-167137/ RTF0167136-01122585

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/ .

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here .

Role Description

About the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division
: The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise of the SFPUC is responsible for the management of approximately 61,000 acres of Bay Area watershed lands under SFPUC ownership as well as 150 miles of utility right-of-way. The NRLM Division is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on these lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System which serves 2.7 million customers. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations. We strive to become a leader in science-based and collaborative environmental stewardship in order to continue providing high-quality and reliable drinking water to our customers.

About The Position

The Programs and Operations Manager provides daily oversight, leadership and strategic direction for the Alameda Creek Watershed Center (ACWC) , advancing its mission as a hub for public education, community engagement, and watershed stewardship. This position oversees daily operations, including the establishment of clear policies and procedures that support safe, consistent, and high quality operations. The Manager supervises staff and volunteers, fostering a high performing and inclusive team environment. The Manager will be a visible, approachable, and supportive leader who builds trust, develops staff, encourages collaboration, and fosters a positive workplace culture where employees and volunteers can thrive. This position is responsible for overseeing the development of high quality educational and interpretive programs, and ensuring a welcoming and meaningful experience for all visitors. The Manager plays a leadership role in shaping the Center’s public identity, developing partnerships, and leading community engagement efforts that support SFPUC’s mission of service, stewardship, and equity. This position works collaboratively across the Division and the SFPUC on planning and programming efforts that strengthen public understanding of the Alameda Creek Watershed, local ecology, cultural history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. The role requires initiative, sound judgment, and a commitment to equity, public service, and environmental stewardship.

Work Schedule:
Tuesday through Saturday with occasional work on evenings and Sundays for special events, subject to change if necessary.

Working Relationship:
This position will report to the Alameda Watershed Resources Manager and will supervise a team of staff and volunteers. Initially this position will supervise the ACWC Facility Coordinator and the Education and Volunteers Coordinator, along with 6 part-time staff and several volunteers. This position will require professional, welcoming and friendly interactions with the public and community/agency partners. This position will require collaboration with the facilities team, communications, staff and managers throughout the division, key staff in PUC, including the Assistant General Manager for the Water Enterprise.

Nature of Work:
Portion of the work duties will be outdoors, exposing the incumbent to inclement weather, potential hazards, and animals common in a natural landscape. The position may stand and/or walk for extended periods of time. Ability to work in a busy, noisy environment. Occasionally may lift and/or push 30 pounds of equipment.

Essential duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategic Operations and Facility Management

Provide daily oversight of facility operations to ensure a safe, welcoming, and mission aligned visitor experience.
Lead the development and implementation of operational policies and procedures that guide facility use, visitor services, safety practices, and daily operations.
Oversee the aquarium, exhibits, grounds, and community spaces to ensure safe, high quality and consistent standards.
Direct the care, protection, and organization of collections and interpretive materials.
Oversee safety, security, and emergency preparedness efforts in alignment with SFPUC policies and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate maintenance and repairs with the facilities team and contractors, proactively identifying operational needs and improvements.

Interpretation, Education, and Program Leadership

Provide leadership for the development and delivery of interpretive, educational, and public programs that support SFPUC goals and community needs.
Establish interpretive themes related to watershed ecology, cultural and tribal history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System.
Develop program guidelines, procedures, and quality standards to ensure consistency and excellence across offerings.
Evaluate program effectiveness and develop summary reports using data and community feedback, supporting continuous improvement.
Maintain subject matter expertise in regional natural and cultural history and SFPUC systems.

Community Engagement and Partnership Development

Lead outreach, community engagement, and communications strategies that increase visibility and participation in ACWC programs.
Build and sustain partnerships with public agencies, schools, community based organizations, tribal representatives and local governments.
Represent the ACWC, the Division, and the SFPUC at public meetings, professional conferences, and community events.
Support initiatives that strengthen community relationships, advance equity, and expand access to programs and services.

Staff and Volunteer Leadership

Build and maintain staff capacity to ensure the ACWC is fully and reliably staffed for public operating hours, programs, and special events
Develop staff guidelines, volunteer protocols, and workflow procedures to support consistent operations.
Lead staff development, performance management, scheduling, and training.
Oversee volunteer recruitment, onboarding, training, and engagement programs.
Provide coaching, and support to staff and volunteers, promoting a collaborative, inclusive, and service oriented culture.

Administration and Strategic Planning

Manage budgets, contracts, procurement, and HR related processes in alignment with SFPUC policies.
Develop and maintain administrative policies and procedures that support efficient, compliant, and transparent operations.
Contribute to strategic planning and the development of long term goals, policies, and operational plans for the Division and SFPUC.
Prepare reports and performance metrics that support accountability and continuous improvement.

Ideal Candidate And Competencies

The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated track record and ability to exercise the following leadership competencies which are critical for success in the role of Alameda and Tuolumne Watershed Resources Manager at SFPUC's Natural Resources & Lands Management Division.

Relationship Management: Builds open, honest, and respectful relationships through effective communication and collaboration techniques. Develops networks and lasting partnerships across boundaries to maintain strategic relationships and achieve common goals. Utilizes a variety of communication approaches to successfully gain support, influence others, and strengthen relationship.

How To Qualify

Minimum Qualifications:
Minimum qualifications reflect the lowest level of acceptable education and/or experience required of an individual such that the individual reasonably could be expected to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position. Candidates must meet all the requirements established by the MQs to be considered for the position.

Education: Possession of a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university
Experience: Five (5) years of professional work experience coordinating or directing environmental stewardship, education or related community programs in visitor services, educational programming, interpretive center operations, or community engagement; Experience managing budgets, contracts, or administrative processes and collaborating with community partners, public agencies, educators, or local governments.
License: Possession of a valid and current California driver’s license.

Substitution:
Additional qualifying professional experience may substitute for the education requirement on a year for year basis for up to 2 years. One (1) year is equivalent to thirty (30) semester units/forty-five (45) quarter units.

Note: One year of full-time employment is equivalent to 2000 hours. (2000 hours of qualifying work experience is based on a 40-hour work week.)

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted. Applicants who meet the minimum qualifications are not guaranteed to advance through all of the steps in the selection process.

Desirable Qualifications

The stated desirable qualifications may be used to identify job finalists at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred for hiring.

Supervisory experience with staff and volunteers interacting with the public.
Experience developing or implementing policies, procedures, or standard operating guidelines for community, non-profit or public facilities, such as visitor centers or education centers.
Experience supporting operations for a community facility (opening/closing, safety procedures, coordinating maintenance and repairs).
Experience representing and working within a public agency or large governmental or nonprofit organization, such as a park agency, public utility or municipal government.
Leadership experience in supporting interpretive centers or environmental education programs.
Experience developing interpretive exhibits, educational materials, or public programs.
Knowledge of California natural and cultural history, ideally focused on the Diablo Range and Bay Area, including the regional geography, plants and animals.
Experience in community engagement and outreach.
Knowledge of and experience working with local tribes.
Experience collaborating with regional Bay Area community and environmental organizations.
Experience managing contracts.
Experience building partnerships with diverse communities and supporting equitable access to public services.

Every application is reviewed to ensure that you meet the mini

About the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division
: The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise of the SFPUC is responsible for the management of approximately 61,000 acres of Bay Area watershed lands under SFPUC ownership as well as 150 miles of utility right-of-way. The NRLM Division is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on these lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System which serves 2.7 million customers. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations. We strive to become a leader in science-based and collaborative environmental stewardship in order to continue providing high-quality and reliable drinking water to our customers.

About The Position

The Programs and Operations Manager provides daily oversight, leadership and strategic direction for the Alameda Creek Watershed Center (ACWC), advancing its mission as a hub for public education, community engagement, and watershed stewardship. This position oversees daily operations, including the establishment of clear policies and procedures that support safe, consistent, and high quality operations. The Manager supervises staff and volunteers, fostering a high performing and inclusive team environment. The Manager will be a visible, approachable, and supportive leader who builds trust, develops staff, encourages collaboration, and fosters a positive workplace culture where employees and volunteers can thrive. The Manager plays a leadership role in shaping the Center’s public identity, developing partnerships, and leading community engagement efforts that support SFPUC’s mission of service, stewardship, and equity. This position will require professional, welcoming and friendly interactions with the public and community/agency partners. This position will require collaboration with the facilities team, communications, staff and managers throughout the division, key staff in PUC, including the Assistant General Manager for the Water Enterprise.

Portion of the work duties will be outdoors, exposing the incumbent to inclement weather, potential hazards, and animals common in a natural landscape. The position may stand and/or walk for extended periods of time. Ability to work in a busy, noisy environment. Occasionally may lift and/or push 30 pounds of equipment.
